w03.final_b0_work_seconds_note: Mean of 3 independent post-hoc confirmation probes at this exact frozen n (2.007788, 2.034665, 2.030194), run 2026-09-20 to investigate a data-integrity anomaly -- see calibration_anomaly_note below. The ORIGINAL calibration run's single confirm probe for this n reported 1.962438s, IDENTICAL to 6 decimal places to that same run's w05 confirm value despite being a different workload, different scratch directory, and a different subprocess -- investigated directly (see note), never reproduced, root cause not found. All values across every probe (original 1.962438s; this run's 2.007788/2.034665/2.030194s) are comfortably within workload-catalog.tsv's 1-5s target band, so the frozen n itself is not in question -- only the single original data point was untrustworthy.
w03.calibration_anomaly_note: A review of this pilot pass found calibration_result.json's original w03 and w05 'final_b0_work_seconds' fields were BIT-IDENTICAL floats (1.962438) despite being independent measurements of different workloads in different scratch directories via different subprocess invocations -- a physical impossibility for two real, independent Time.get_ticks_usec() measurements. Investigated by (1) re-running both single confirm probes fresh (got 2.077743 and 1.94432 respectively -- immediately different, so NOT a reproducible artifact of this machine/workload), and (2) running calibrate.py fully from scratch (got yet another distinct pair, 1.963992/1.9916). No code path was found that could explain the original duplication (different scratch dirs via setup_scratch_project's rmtree+rebuild rule out stale-file reuse; different filenames work_time_w03.txt vs work_time_w05.txt rule out a shared-file collision). Resolution: the frozen n's (which predate this anomaly and were already independently exercised by the real 200-row pilot showing normal per-condition variance) were reconfirmed via fresh, independent probes instead of trusting the original suspect single data point or re-freezing to a recalibration run's slightly different solved n. This does NOT affect pilot_results.tsv's validity -- that data was never derived from this JSON file's suspect field, only from the frozen n itself, which multiple independent re-probes confirm behaves as expected.

fit.note: fit diagnostics (floor/slope/probes) are from the ORIGINAL calibration run that solved n=15667413 -- only that run's single-probe 'final_b0_work_seconds' summary field was suspect, not the fit itself, which is corroborated by the frozen n's real behavior in the pilot and in post-hoc reprobes.
